How it began

Every festival starts as something smaller

Festival of Ideas didn't begin as a festival. It began the way most good ideas do — quietly, and a little unsure of itself. Here's how it grew wings.

Egg

A question left in the margins

It started with a handful of readers who kept scribbling questions in the margins of everything they read — and wondered why campus had no room to ask them out loud.

Caterpillar

Feeding on borrowed pages

The question grew on shared drafts, late-night reading circles and long arguments about books — slowly turning from a passing thought into something worth building.

Chrysalis

Months of quiet restructuring

Behind closed doors, the idea reorganised itself — a name, a shape, a purpose. What looked like nothing happening was, in fact, the hardest part.

Butterfly

Festival of Ideas takes flight

What emerged was never just an event — a festival built to give every unfinished thought a stage, a page, and an audience willing to listen.

Ideas rarely arrive whole. They molt, again and again, until they're ready to fly.

What's on

Sessions worth clearing your calendars for

Author readings

Writers reading from work in progress and work long finished, in their own voice.

Panel discussions

Editors, critics and authors in conversation on craft, publishing and everything between.

Fireside conversations

Closed-room chats on history, geopolitics and the decisions shaping what comes next.

Ignition talks

Founders, scientists, policymakers and historians on the ideas reshaping how nations think and grow.

Writing workshops

Small, hands-on rooms led by working writers — bring an unfinished draft.

Interactive sessions

Live polls, games and open floors that pull the audience into the programme, not just the seats.
